archetype.name: Dual-Threat (developing)
archetype.definition: A second-year, first-round passer whose rookie value came as much from designed runs and scrambles as from the pocket, and who opened 2026 throwing with a precision he never showed as a rookie.

report.headline: One brilliant September game, then injured reserve and a fall to QB3
report.take:
Jaxson Dart's 2026 line reads like an MVP's: first among 49 qualifiers in EPA per dropback (0.578), completion rate and TD rate, no interceptions, no lost fumbles. Almost all of it comes from one afternoon. In Week 1 against Dallas, now the league's 31st-ranked defense, he went 23 of 29 for 230 yards and three scores with 54 rushing yards, a 21.9 EPA game. Against the Rams in Week 2 he played 12% of the snaps before getting hurt. Jameis Winston then started four games and J.J. McCarthy two. Dart is on injured reserve and listed third on the depth chart, so the season-long ranks describe one good game against a weak defense rather than a level of play.

That Week 1 game still tells you something. As a rookie he was a run-first creator: third in the league in rushing yards (487), with a CPOE of -0.2 and bad throws on 15% of attempts. Against Dallas he got the ball out faster (2.64 seconds against 2.82 last year), threw a bit more aggressively, and was accurate underneath and in the 10-19 yard window. He completed 13 of 14 short throws and averaged 1.167 EPA on 11 intermediate attempts. His 9 third-down throws converted 88.9% of the time, and all 7 red-zone throws were successes, three of them touchdowns. Isaiah Likely did the most damage, averaging 1.357 EPA per target.

The tiny sample hides a few things. He threw deep three times and missed all three. The red-zone and third-down perfection will not repeat at that rate on any real volume. His pressure-to-sack rate (33.3%, 29th of 42) is close to last year's 36.5%, which ranked 43rd of 62. That is a habit he has carried since his rookie year: holding the ball while trying to extend plays. His rushing is the most durable part of his profile. Designed runs went for 8.17 yards a carry, consistent with a rookie season built on his legs.

The outlook is about his role more than his talent. Harbaugh's offense passes 7.5 points below expectation (29th) and the line allows hits at the third-worst rate. Winston and McCarthy have both started ahead of him. Even once healthy, Dart needs an opening, most plausibly a McCarthy injury (he is questionable with a hip bruise), to get back on the field. If he does, his rookie floor of rushing value plus whatever accuracy gain proves real makes him a usable starter. Judging from one game against a bottom-two defense, his accuracy is unproven.

strengths.title: Rushing as a reliable baseline
strengths.body: He was third in rushing yards among QBs as a rookie. In his one full 2026 game he ran 11 times for 54 yards, and his designed runs were never stuffed. The legs, not the passing ranks, are what make him a viable fantasy and real-football starter when he plays. That trait has held across both seasons, so it should survive a return from injury, assuming the injury isn't to a lower body part.

strengths.title: Sharper short-to-intermediate accuracy
strengths.body: His tracking CPOE jumped from slightly below zero as a rookie to double digits, and his bad-throw rate fell. Most of the gain came on throws under 20 yards, where he paired a quicker release with on-time ball placement. It is a plausible second-year step, but it rests on 34 attempts, one of them against a defense ranked 31st.

strengths.title: Finishing drives in Week 1
strengths.body: All seven of his red-zone throws were successes, three for touchdowns, and his third-down throws moved the chains almost every time. That is execution against a bad defense, not a repeatable rate. It does show he can work the tight ends and backs in tight areas, with Likely the main beneficiary.

concerns.title: Injured and buried at QB3
concerns.body: He is on injured reserve, did not practice, and sits third on the depth chart behind two QBs who have each started. The 12% snap share in Week 2 was the last time he played. No return date is listed, so any rebound depends both on health and on the coaches choosing him.

concerns.title: Sample inflated by Dallas
concerns.body: Nearly every number comes from one game against the league's 31st-ranked defense. His only snaps against a top defense, the Rams (4th), produced negative EPA. Ranking first among 49 in EPA per dropback on two games says more about the schedule than about him.

concerns.title: Sacks and the missing deep game
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate is still among the worst, as it was in 2025. That is the cost of a play-extender holding the ball, made worse by a line that ranks 30th in hit rate allowed. He also missed all three deep attempts, so the vertical part of his game is unproven this year.

trend.note: He opened with a 21.9-EPA win over Dallas, then left Week 2 after 12% of the snaps. Since then he has gone to injured reserve while Winston and McCarthy took every start.

nextGame.headline: Soft Washington matchup, but Dart isn't expected to play
nextGame.body:
On paper this is a good draw for a mobile passer. Washington allows the fifth-most QB fantasy points a game (28th of 32), ranks 26th in defensive success rate, and gives up the most production to opposing top tight ends, which fits the Likely-heavy approach Dart used in Week 1. Defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw are both out for the year, weakening the interior rush. Washington does limit explosive runs (2nd) and short passes (7th), so the yards would come from sustained drives rather than big plays. Rain is possible, but the forecast is light drizzle and mild wind, a small factor at most.

The availability that matters most is Dart's own. He is on injured reserve and third on the depth chart, so he is not a realistic option this week. McCarthy is questionable with a hip bruise and was limited Monday. If McCarthy can't go, Winston, who started four games, is the more likely replacement than Dart. For the Giants' offense, Cam Skattebo is out and Darnell Mooney is questionable, which thins a run-leaning attack. The Book has the Giants as 2.5-point favorites with a 42.5 total.

keyMatchups.title: Washington is generous to quarterbacks
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks 28th in QB fantasy points allowed and 27th in passing TDs allowed a game. Whoever starts for New York gets a favorable setup, which is why the depth chart matters more than the matchup for Dart.

keyMatchups.title: Top tight ends feast here
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks last at holding lead tight ends to their averages. Likely was Dart's most productive target in Week 1, and that edge goes to whichever QB starts.

keyMatchups.title: McCarthy's hip decides the QB order
keyMatchups.body: McCarthy is questionable and was limited Monday. His status, not Dart's, sets who starts, and Dart is still the third option behind Winston.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dart is designated to return from injured reserve and practices, and where he lands on the depth chart relative to Winston if McCarthy's hip lingers.

restOfSeason.body:
For now, the most likely outcome is that Dart sees little or no meaningful action until he is both healthy and moved back up a depth chart that currently has him third. If he does start again, expect something between his rookie self and his Week 1 self. The rushing (roughly 25-45 yards a start) is the sustainable part, since it carried him to a top-three finish among QBs as a rookie.

The accuracy gain is plausible but small-sample, and the passing volume will be modest. This is a run-leaning Harbaugh offense with a line that allows hits, so 170-225 passing yards a start is a fair band. The red-zone and third-down perfection and the zero-interception line will regress toward his rookie rates, which included interceptions and plenty of sacks. These projections apply to games he starts, not to every remaining week.
swingFactors: His return from injured reserve and how healthy he looks
McCarthy's hip and the coaches' order between Winston and Dart
Whether the Week 1 accuracy holds against better defenses

confidence.note: Two games, one a partial, on injured reserve as QB3
